newsitem.title: UK: APV more confident after tough 1996.
newsitem.headline: APV more confident after tough 1996.

text.p: British engineering and components group APV Plc said on Thursday that it was in a better position to improve its financial performance in 1997 and beyond.
The group conceded that its financial performance in 1996 did not meet its objectives as it disclosed that pre-tax profits fell to 15.0 million stg in that year from 26.9 million in 1995.

"The continuing drive to reduce our cost base ensures that, despite stiff competition and uncertain market conditions, we are better positioned to deliver improved performance in 1997 and beyond," said chairman Mike Smith in a statement.
APV also said orders at the start of this year were higher in value and margin that at the same period in 1996.
This follows on from a general improvement in the group's underlying performance in the second half of 1996 after a tough first half in a weak market.
In response to the poor trading conditions seen in the first few months of 1996, the company implemented cost reduction measures across the group.
APV plans to pay a final dividend of 1.7p per share, making an unchanged total for the year of 2.7p per share. By 1200 GMT, its shares had risen 4-1/2p to stand at 68p.
